title: Impact of lidocain administration on hemodynamics during anesthesia
summary: Lidocaine has been used as an analgesic during surgery since the middle of the 20th century. It is known that lidocaine administration can reduce the need for analgesics and lower the incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). This is particularly true for use during and after general anesthesia. Up to now, the influence of such lidocaine administration on circulatory parameters (e.g. blood pressure or heart rhythm) has hardly been systematically investigated. The aim of this study is to analyze the association between intraoperative application of lidocaine (with the aim to reduce pain) and cardiocirculatory relevant events (e.g. spontaneous decrease of blood pressure). The analysis is limited to specific gynecological surgical procedures. For this purpose, routinely collected data will be analysed retrospectively.

interventions.name:
female patients (≥ 18 years) undergoing specific gynaecological surgery under general anesthesia:
with intraoperative, intravenous lidocaine administration

female patients (≥ 18 years) undergoing specific gynaecological surgery under general anesthesia:
without intraoperative, intravenous lidocaine administration

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
> age ≥ 18 years
> female sex
> ASA-Score I to III
> specific gynecological surgery under general anesthesia (see section health condition/problem)
> surgery between 01.01.2013 to 31.12.2021
Exclusion criteria:
> ASA-Score IV and V
> heart pacemaker
> known allergy to local anesthetics
